sections.h2: How is Nevada organized when you sell a house here?
sections.html:
Nevada has 16 counties and one independent city, Carson City, which merged with the old Ormsby County in 1969. Clark County is by far the largest. Its 2020 population was 2,407,226, while Esmeralda County had 729 residents.

That split matters for a seller, because the county is where your deed is recorded, your tax bill is issued and your property is valued. Each county has an assessor, a treasurer and a recorder. The names of the offices are the same statewide, but the rules about rates and fees can change by county.

Our local pages follow the same structure. Start with the county guide for your area, such as the Clark County property tax guide or the Washoe County property tax guide, then move to the city page. Carson City has its own guide as a consolidated city and county.

sections.h2: What does a seller owe at the county level?
sections.html:
Property tax on a Nevada house is due on the third Monday of August. If the bill is over $100, you can split it into four roughly equal payments, due on the third Monday of August, then the first Mondays of October, January and March (NRS 361.483).

The assessor values the property, the treasurer collects the money and the recorder files your deed. A sale usually touches all three offices, so call them early if something looks off. Our Nevada property tax guide walks through appeals and exemptions.

Who to call:

  • Assessor, for value, exemptions and ownership questions.
  • Treasurer, for the payoff on unpaid taxes.
  • Recorder, for deed filing and transfer tax questions.

Phone numbers and hours change, so confirm them on the county website before you drive over.

sections.h2: How much is the real property transfer tax?
sections.html:
Nevada charges a transfer tax on each deed worth more than $100, and it is figured per $500 of value. The state statute sets a base rate that depends on county size, plus a flat state add-on.

ItemRate per $500 of valueSource
Base tax, county with 700,000 or more people (Clark)$1.25NRS 375.020
Base tax, county under 700,000 people$0.65NRS 375.020
Additional state tax, all counties$1.30NRS 375.023
Optional county add-on, smaller countiesUp to $0.05NRS 375.026

Add the first two rows for Clark County and the tax is $2.55 per $500 before any local amounts. For a county under 700,000 it is $1.95. The statute lets buyer and seller agree on who pays, but the county can collect from either one, so both are liable (NRS 375.030). Ask the recorder or your closing agent for the exact figure on your deal.

sections.h2: Is foreclosure judicial in Nevada, and how long does it take?
sections.html:
Most Nevada foreclosures are non-judicial. A deed of trust usually contains a power of sale, so the trustee can sell the home at auction without a court case. The statute does not prohibit a judicial foreclosure either (NRS 107.085).

The steps run in a fixed order:

  • The trustee records a notice of default and election to sell and mails it to the owner.
  • The owner has 35 days after that mailing and recording to make good the missed amount.
  • At least 3 months must pass after the notice is recorded before a sale can happen.
  • The notice of sale is posted for 20 days and published once a week for 3 weeks.

After the sale there is no right of redemption, since a trustee sale passes the owner's title to the buyer (NRS 107.080). For owner-occupied homes, you can petition the district court for foreclosure mediation within 30 days after service, with a $25 filing fee, unless you waive it (NRS 107.086). The selling window is before the auction. See the Nevada tax sale page if the lien is for taxes instead of a loan.

sections.h2: What happens to an inherited house in Nevada?
sections.html:
The route depends on the size of the estate and on whether the house is in it. A house is real property, so the quick affidavit route is usually closed. That route requires that the decedent left no Nevada real property, and the amount is capped at $150,000 for a surviving spouse and $25,000 for anyone else (NRS 146.080).

RouteLimitStatute
Affidavit, no real property$150,000 spouse, $25,000 othersNRS 146.080
Set aside without administrationEstate of $150,000 or lessNRS 146.070
Summary administration$500,000 or less after liensNRS 145.040

A set-aside petition cannot start until 30 days after death, and values are measured as of the date of death after enforceable liens. Larger estates go through regular administration. Heirs who plan to sell should read our Nevada probate guide and speak with a probate attorney first. If the owner recorded a deed upon death, the house may pass outside probate, which is covered on our transfer on death deed page.

sections.h2: What does Nevada's homestead law protect?
sections.html:
The homestead exemption shields up to $605,000 of equity in a home from a forced sale to creditors, unless allodial title has been established (NRS 115.010). It does not protect against a mortgage, a deed of trust or a lien for taxes, and nothing in the chapter exempts property from a tax sale (NRS 115.080).

A declaration has to be signed, acknowledged and recorded like a deed. If the home is one spouse's separate property, both spouses must sign it. A homestead is not treated as abandoned until a written declaration is recorded (NRS 115.040). If a creditor forces a sale, the $605,000 paid to the owner stays protected only if it is put into another homestead that is identified within 45 days and occupied within 180 days (NRS 115.055). Details are on our homestead exemption page.

sections.h2: What must a Nevada seller disclose?
sections.html:
Nevada requires a written condition disclosure on residential property with one to four dwelling units. The seller completes the form, and at least 10 days before the conveyance the seller or the seller's agent must serve it on the buyer. An agent may not fill it out for the seller (NRS 113.130).

Points that catch sellers off guard:

  • You only disclose defects you know about. The law does not require you to disclose what you are unaware of (NRS 113.140).
  • A completed form is not a warranty.
  • If you skip the form, the buyer can cancel before closing.
  • A seller who conveys without disclosing a known defect can owe the buyer treble the repair cost, plus fees (NRS 113.150).

Sales by foreclosure are exempt, as are certain transfers between spouses and relatives and sales by a fiduciary acting for a deceased or incapacitated owner. In Clark County, a seller of a new residence also has to give gaming enterprise district information. An as-is sale does not remove the duty to be honest about what you know, but it does mean the buyer is not asking you to fix anything.

sections.h2: What if a tenant lives in the house you want to sell?
sections.html:
The lease stays in place. When a rented property is sold voluntarily, the new owner takes over the landlord's rights and duties under the rental agreement, unless the buyer and tenant agree to change or end it (NRS 118A.349). The seller must transfer the security deposit, and the new owner must send the tenant a notice within 30 days giving payment contact details and the deposit amount.

So a buyer who wants the house empty needs the tenant's agreement or a lawful notice process, and a cash buyer will price in that timeline. Read our Nevada landlord and tenant guide before you promise anyone a move-out date. If someone is living in a house without permission and has no lease, see the squatters and adverse possession page.

sections.h2: What does a cash sale as-is look like in Nevada?
sections.html:
It means the buyer pays without a mortgage and takes the house in its current condition, so there is no appraisal contingency and no repair list from a lender. You still sign a purchase agreement, open escrow and record a deed, and you still complete the disclosure form for any known defects.

Before closing, expect these items on your side of the table:

  • A payoff for any mortgage, deed of trust or tax lien.
  • Your share of the transfer tax, if the contract says so.
  • A clean answer on who occupies the house.

Our city pages cover the local details for Las Vegas, Reno, Henderson and the rest of the state. Heirs can also review our estate tax page. For anything that depends on your facts, ask a Nevada attorney or the county office before you sign.

faqs.q: How many counties does Nevada have?
faqs.a: Sixteen, plus one independent city, Carson City. Clark County, which includes Las Vegas, is the most populous.

faqs.q: When are Nevada property taxes due?
faqs.a: On the third Monday of August. Bills over $100 can be paid in four installments, due in August, October, January and March.
Mostly no. A deed of trust power of sale lets a trustee sell, but at least 3 months must pass after the notice of default is recorded, and there is no redemption after the sale.

faqs.q: How much is the transfer tax?
faqs.a: Under the statutes, $2.55 per $500 of value in Clark County and $1.95 per $500 in counties under 700,000 people. Local add-ons may apply, so ask the recorder.

faqs.q: Do I disclose problems in an as-is sale?
faqs.a: Yes. Sellers of one to four unit homes must serve a disclosure form listing known defects at least 10 days before conveyance.

faqs.q: Can I sell an inherited house before probate ends?
faqs.a: Usually the court-appointed personal representative has the authority. A recorded deed upon death may let the beneficiary skip probate.

faqs.q: What happens to a tenant when I sell?
faqs.a: The lease continues with the new owner unless both agree otherwise. The new owner must notify the tenant within 30 days.

faqs.q: How much equity does the homestead exemption protect?
faqs.a: Up to $605,000 from most creditors, but not from a mortgage foreclosure or a tax sale.
